plan.melodySummary: The melody opens intimately in the clarinet over a soft double bass pad, then passes to the piccolo as the texture blooms, before the trombone shoulders the tune through the two-thirds climax with the piccolo soaring above in countermelody. The dynamic arc rises in waves from a hushed !p! opening through a !ff! climax around mm.17-24, then settles back to a warm, resolved !mp! close.

sections.label: Phrase A — Awakening
sections.notes: Begin at !p!, long-breathed and legato; let each phrase float over the sustained pad, no accent. Trombone pad is softer, !pp!.

sections.label: Phrase B — First Swell
sections.notes: Enter at !mp! and swell toward !mf! by m.16; bright and singing, riding the rising line. Clarinet weaves a gentle countermelody beneath, kept at !mp! or softer.

sections.label: Phrase C — Climax
sections.notes: The big arrival: play broad and !ff!, octave-strong and noble. Piccolo soars ABOVE with a descant countermelody at !f!; Double Bass reinforces every downbeat firmly.

sections.label: Phrase D — Resolution
sections.notes: Pull back to a warm !mp!, tender and unhurried; ritard slightly into m.32 for a settled cadence. Trombone offers soft sustained counter-lines at !p!, bass drops to a low pedal.

Piccolo.instruction: Rest in the opening and closing phrases. Carry the melody brightly at !mp!-!mf! in mm.9-16, then rise above the climax (mm.17-24) as a soaring descant countermelody at !f!, never covering the trombone tune.

Clarinet.instruction: Open the piece with a hushed, legato melody at !p!. In mm.9-16 drop to a supporting countermelody (!mp! or softer), thin harmony at the climax, then reclaim the tune tenderly at !mp! for the resolution.

Trombone.instruction: Provide soft sustained pads (!pp!-!p!) under the outer phrases. Seize the melody broadly and nobly at !ff! through the two-thirds climax (mm.17-24), then return to warm counter-lines at !p! in the close.

Double Bass.instruction: Anchor the whole arrangement with sustained low pads, swelling with the dynamic arc: !pp! at the start, firm downbeat reinforcement at the !ff! climax, and a settled low pedal at !mp! for the ending.
